title: A Noetherian zero-dimensional scheme has finite discrete underlying space
statement: Let $Y$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth] [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] whose underlying topological space has Krull dimension $\dim Y\le 0$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then $|Y|$ is a finite discrete space: every point is closed and every singleton is open. The assertion includes $Y=\varnothing$.

proof.text: The underlying topological space $|Y|$ is Noetherian (every nonempty set of closed subsets has a minimal element) by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], $Y$ is quasi-separated; therefore [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-scheme-spectral] applies to the quasi-compact scheme $Y$ and gives that $|Y|$ is spectral, in particular sober [def-weil-spectral-space]. A sober space is $T_0$: if $x\ne y$ lay in exactly the same open subsets, then $\overline{\{x\}}=\overline{\{y\}}$ would be an irreducible closed subset with two generic points $x$ and $y$, contradicting uniqueness.

Apply [lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-closed-finite] to the closed subset $Z=|Y|$ of the T0 Noetherian space $|Y|$. The hypothesis $\dim Y\le0$ is exactly the required bound on $\dim Z$, so $|Y|$ is finite and every singleton is closed.

A finite space in which every singleton is closed is discrete: for any point $y$, the complement of $\{y\}$ is a finite union of closed singletons and hence closed, so $\{y\}$ is open. The empty space satisfies the same conclusion vacuously.
